alarms.title: AI weld monitor flags undercut that is not there
alarms.operator_message: The AI sees possible undercut on the left edge. It is only medium sure.
alarms.technical_detail: In-process seam-camera classifier during welding: undercut, confidence 0.58, at 40-55 mm. The heatmap focuses on a bright arc reflection on the bead. The laser profile at the same spot shows no undercut (0.05 mm, limit 0.5 mm).

ai_decision.what: Possible undercut on the left edge, 40-55 mm from the start

ground_truth.root_cause: Arc glare on a shiny spot fooled the camera model (false alarm).
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Weld stopped and part reworked for no reason.

expected_response.resolved_when: Operator overrules the AI with a reason and the weld continues.

hints: The AI can be fooled by light reflections. Check before you act.
Look where the heatmap is red and compare with the bead profile at the same place.
If the profile and your eyes show no undercut, press 'AI was wrong' and accept the part.

alarms.literature: Image-based defect CNNs and Grad-CAM explanations: Zhang et al. 2026; Satsangi et al. 2026. Trust calibration: van der Waa et al. 2021.
resolution_script: Open the heatmap: the red spot is on a bright reflection.
Open the bead profile at the same place: depth 0.05 mm, limit 0.5 mm.
Look at the bead yourself. No undercut means the AI was wrong.
Press 'Problem solved' and write what you saw, e.g. 'reflection'.

alarms.title: AI weld monitor is unsure: unfamiliar material
alarms.operator_message: The AI says the weld looks OK. But it has never seen this material.
alarms.technical_detail: In-process bead classifier (seam camera + arc signals): OK, confidence 0.61, with an out-of-distribution warning. The zinc-coated surface and spatter pattern are outside the training range. Galvanised steel is prone to porosity from zinc vapour.

ground_truth.root_cause: Model trained only on plain steel; zinc vapour is causing fine pores it cannot recognise.

hints: 'Unfamiliar' means the AI is guessing. Do not trust its OK.
This material was not in the examples the AI learned from.
Send the part to manual inspection and note that the material was new for the AI.

alarms.literature: Models fail when material or setup changes: Georgousis et al. 2026; Zhang et al. 2026 (generalisation).
resolution_script: Do not trust this 'OK': the AI has not seen this material.
Read the warning: galvanised steel was not in its examples.
Let the weld finish, then mark it 'Check needed'.
Send it to manual inspection and say the AI was unsure.
Press 'Problem solved' and write 'sent to inspection'.

alarms.title: AI camera misses pores that the arc signals show
alarms.operator_title: AI result and arc signals do not match
alarms.operator_message: The AI camera says OK. But the arc signals show gas pores forming.
alarms.technical_detail: Cross-check mismatch during welding: the camera-based bead classifier says OK (0.91) from the surface. The arc-voltage signal shows repeated short drops, typical of gas pores forming below the surface. Surface images cannot see internal pores.

ground_truth.root_cause: Internal porosity from a disturbed gas shield; the AI camera only sees the surface.
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Weak weld delivered; the AI keeps being trusted for defects it cannot see.

expected_response.resolved_when: Weld marked for X-ray inspection and the AI miss recorded.

hints: The arc signals count here, not the camera. The camera cannot see inside the weld.
Check the gas flow and the nozzle for spatter.
Mark the weld for X-ray inspection and record that the AI missed it.

alarms.literature: Internal defects need radiographic/ultrasonic testing: Zhang et al. 2026; cross-check design: docs/04.
resolution_script: Trust the arc signals here, not the AI camera.
The camera only sees the surface. Pores form inside.
Check the gas flow and clean the nozzle.
Mark this weld 'Check needed' for X-ray inspection.
Press 'Problem solved' and write 'pores, AI missed them'.
